name: Tarbhfheis

attributes.attribute: a way to name the next king

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tarbhfheis is the Irish name for the rite of bull-sleep. Bull-sleep was a way of finding the next king. A seer ate the flesh of a bull and lay down to sleep in the bull's skin. In a dream the seer could see the man who was to rule. The rite is a form of divination.

okr.objective: Describe Tarbhfheis, the older name for bull-sleep.
key_results: Tarbhfheis is the Irish name for bull-sleep.
It was used to pick the next king.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
